correctness.rationale: Writing the published operators as \(\beta(R)=R\circ\leq\) and \(\delta(R)=R\circ\leq^{-1}\), their composites are \(R\circ\leq^{-1}\circ\leq\) and \(R\circ\leq\circ\leq^{-1}\). Universal commutation is therefore exactly equality of the common-lower and common-upper relations. The proof that this common relation is the comparability-component equivalence, plus finite iteration of common bounds to component endpoints, is complete. Exhaustive checks over all posets through four points and all binary relations through three points corroborate the theorem.

value.rationale: Sato's paper uses separate box-only and diamond-only condensation procedures as a substantive normalization tool. The accepted theorem gives the exact finite condition under which those procedures are compatible, identifies the canonical joint normal form, and shows that both confluence conditions survive the completion. This is a natural structural extension rather than a routine restatement.
